senses.gloss:
सौमिक सौमिक, अस्, ई, अम्, (fr. सोम), per-
formed with Soma juice (said of an oblation or
sacrifice), relating to the Soma juice; relating to
Soma or the moon, lunar; (ई), f. a particular sacrifice
performed on the day of full moon (= दीक्षणी-
येष्टि).

सौमदत्ति सौमदत्ति, इस्, m. (fr. सोम-
दत्त), a patronymic.

सौमनस सौमनस, अस्, आ or ई, अम् (fr. सु-
मनस्), agreeable to the feelings, pleasing; relating
to flowers, floral, flowery; (अस्), m., N. of the eighth
day of the civil month (= कर्म-मास); (आ), f. the
outer skin of the nutmeg, = जाती-पत्त्री; (ई), f., N.
of the fifth night of the civil month; (अम्), n.
benevolence, kindness; pleasure, satisfaction.

सौमनस्य, अम्, n. satisfaction of mind, agree-
ableness, enjoyment; a particular offering of flowers
with holy texts placed in the hands of the priest at
a Śrāddha.

सौमनस्यायनी, f. the blossom of the Mālatī
or great-flowering jasmine.

सौमायन सौमायन, अस्, m. (fr. सोम), a
patronymic of Budha; [cf. सौम्य.]

सौमित्र सौमित्र, अस्, m. (fr. सु-मित्रा), a
metronymic of Lakṣmaṇa the younger brother of
Rāma.

सौमित्रि, इस्, m. = सौमित्र above; N. of a
teacher of the Sāma-veda.

सौमिल्ल सौमिल्ल, अस्, m., N. of a dramatic
writer (mentioned in the Mālavikāgnimitra).

सौमेचक सौमेचक, अम्, n. (probably fr.
सु-मेचक), gold.

सौमेधिक सौमेधिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. 5. सु +
मेधा), possessing supernatural knowledge or wis-
dom; (अस्), m. a sage, seer.

सौमेरुक सौमेरुक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. सु-मेरु),
belonging to or coming from Su-meru; (अम्), n. gold.

सौम्य सौम्य, अस्, आ or मी, अम् (fr. सोम),
belonging or relating to Soma or to the moon,
sacred to Soma; having the nature or properties
of Soma; resembling the moon; handsome, pleas-
ing, good, mild, gentle, soft, benign, placid, (सौम्य,
voc. c. ‘O gentle Sir,’ ‘O good Sir,’ used in address-
ing another); auspicious; (अस्), m., N. of Budha or
the planet Mercury (son of Soma); N. of the Vedic
Ṛṣi Budha; a Brāhman (or the proper epithet by
which he should be addressed, see Manu II. 125);
N. of one of the nine Khaṇḍas or divisions of the earth
or of Bharata-varṣa; epithet of the forty-third (or
seventeenth) year of Jupiter's cycle of sixty years;
epithet of certain signs of the zodiac (viz. Taurus,
Cancer, Virgo, Scorpio, Capricornus); the Uḍumbara
fig-tree; the Saumya penance, (see सौम्य-कृच्-
छ्र); (in anatomy) the blood before it becomes
red, serum; the gastric juice; = भास्वर (according
to Śabda-k.); (आस्), m. pl., N. of the five stars in
Orion's head, (also called इल्वल, q. v.); N. of a
class of Pitṛs, (Manu III. 199); (आ), f., N. of
Durgā; a particular metre; the moon-plant, (see
सोम); various other plants, = मल्लिका; = शटी; =
शाल-पर्णी; = गुञ्जा; = महिष-वल्ली; = महा-
ज्योतिष्मती; = रुद्र-जटा; = महेन्द्र-वारुणी;
(अम्), n., scil. अद्भुत, a particular kind of omen
or prodigy (occurring in the Diva or sky).
—सौम्य-
कृच्छ्र, अस्, अम्, m. n. a kind of religious penance
(described as subsisting for five days, severally, on
sesamum, the water of boiled rice, butter-milk
mixed with water, water, and parched grain, and
fasting on the sixth day).
—सौम्य-गन्धी, f. the
Indian white rose.
—सौम्य-ग्रह, अस्, m. an
auspicious or benign planet (such as Mercury, Ju-
piter, Venus, and the full moon).
—सौम्य-ता, f.
or सौम्य-त्व, अम्, n. gentleness, mildness, be-
nignity, placidity; benevolence; beauty.
—सौम्य-
धातु, उस्, m. (according to Śabda-k. f.), the
phlegmatic humor, phlegm.
—सौम्य-नामन्, आ,
म्नी, अ, having a soft or agreeable name (or one
easily pronounced; see Manu III. 10).
—सौम्य-
वपुस्, उस्, उस्, उस्, of an agreeable form.
—सौम्य-
वार, अस्, m. ‘Mercury's day,’ Wednesday.
—सौम्यो-
पचार (˚य-उप्˚), अस्, m. a mild or gentle remedy,
mild measure or means of cure.
